# Compiler Principles

Understand how source text becomes a structured, checked and optimised executable representation.

**Start with the smallest possible example**, calculate a concrete result, explain every symbol, and then examine the assumptions and limitations.

A good compiler course begins with a tiny arithmetic language. We do not need a production parser or LLVM project to understand the grammar, type judgement or optimisation invariant.

## Four lessons

1. [Lexing and Parsing](01-lexing-and-parsing.qmd)
2. [Type Checking and Semantics](02-types-and-semantic-analysis.qmd)
3. [Intermediate Representation and SSA](03-intermediate-representation-and-ssa.qmd)
4. [Optimisation and Correctness](04-optimization-and-correctness.qmd)

## After these lessons

Explain the core example without memorising definitions. Change one assumption and predict what changes in the result. The purpose is to understand the system, not collect terminology.
